original_evidence_metadata.claim: BMI270 CHIP_ID register (address 0x00) expected value: 0x24 -- read and validated once at firmware boot before trusting any further communication with the part
BMI270 CMD register address 0x7E; writing 0xB6 (SOFT_RESET_CMD) triggers a full soft reset; the reference driver waits 2000 µs (2 ms) after issuing it before any further register access

BMI270 PWR_CONF register address 0x7C; bit0 is the advanced-power-save enable -- the part resets into this mode, and it must be written to 0 (disabled) before the configuration-file upload sequence can proceed

BMI270 mandatory configuration-file upload protocol: INIT_CTRL (0x59) ← 0x00 to enable load mode; for each chunk of the config file, write the chunk's **word offset** (byte_index/2) as two bytes to INIT_ADDR_0 (0x5B, low nibble) then INIT_ADDR_1 (0x5C, upper bits) in one transaction, then burst-write the chunk's data bytes to INIT_DATA (0x5E); after all chunks are written, INIT_CTRL ← 0x01 to signal completion. This exact chunked, word-addressed protocol (not a single continuous burst) is required because the device's internal address pointer does not auto-increment across separate I2C transactions

BMI270 INTERNAL_STATUS register address 0x21; configuration-load success is indicated by `(INTERNAL_STATUS & 0x0F) == 0x01` -- must be polled after finishing the upload sequence (DS-IMU-082) rather than assumed instantaneous

BMI270 configuration-file blob exact byte length: 8192, independently counted this session (not trusted from memory/description) by counting hex-byte literals in the array, and cross-checked against the same upstream file's own `dev->config_size = sizeof(bmi270_config_file)` usage. Vendored verbatim into `firmware/bench-imu-01/src/bmi270_config_file.h` -- this project does not and cannot derive this data itself

BMI270 ACC_CONF (0x40) / GYR_CONF (0x42) register addresses; bitfields: ODR = bits[3:0] (100 Hz = 0x08), bandwidth-parameter = bits[6:4] (accel) or bits[5:4] (gyro), performance-mode = bit7 (accel) / bits[7:6] (gyro, noise+filter). This firmware writes ACC_CONF=0xA8 and GYR_CONF=0xE8 (performance-optimized, normal bandwidth, 100 Hz ODR), satisfying REQ-001's >=100 Hz floor

BMI270 PWR_CTRL register address 0x7D; gyroscope-enable = bit1, accelerometer-enable = bit2 (aux_en=bit0 and temp_en=bit3 both left disabled -- no aux sensor on this board, REQ-001 doesn't need temperature). This firmware writes PWR_CTRL=0x06 (gyr_en\|acc_en)

BMI270 accelerometer data starts at ACC_X_LSB=0x0C; gyroscope data starts at GYR_X_LSB=0x12 -- the two 6-byte (X/Y/Z, LSB+MSB each) blocks are contiguous, so a single 12-byte burst read from 0x0C returns a complete accel+gyro sample in one I2C transaction

BMI270_SensorAPI repository license: BSD-3-Clause, permitting redistribution in source form provided the copyright notice, license text, and non-endorsement clause are retained -- satisfied by `firmware/bench-imu-01/src/bmi270_config_file.h`'s full license reproduction, licensing the verbatim vendoring of the 8192-byte configuration blob (DS-IMU-084)

**Full14-pin identities and mode-dependent roles:**1 SDO digital I/O, serial output in SPI4 (I2C address input in I2C);2 ASDx and3 ASCx secondary digital I/O;4 INT1 and9 INT2 digital I/O, including external FIFO-sync input capability;5 VDDIO supply;6 GNDIO and7 GND grounds;8 VDD supply;10 OCSB secondary OIS digital INPUT;11 OSDO secondary OIS digital OUTPUT;12 CSB primary digital input;13 SCx primary digital input, SCK in SPI4/SCL in I2C;14 SDx primary digital I/O, SDI/MOSI input in SPI4, SDA in I2C/SPI3. Pin capability is distinguished from the chosen schematic mode; secondary unused conditions are DS-IMU-095 and SPI4 write high-Z behavior DS-IMU-099. Extends, not silently repurposes, the historical identity-only DS-IMU-077.

CSB internal pull-up to VDDIO: MIN75/TYP100/MAX140kΩ. Interface-pin input capacitance Cin MAX5pF, MIN/TYP unspecified. This does not specify every deselected SDO output's capacitance or establish the aggregate loading, CS edge time, external-bias need or safe clock rate of the actual six-device PCB.

original_evidence_metadata.section: §6.3 Primary Interface Digital Protocol Selection; §1 power-on time
original_evidence_metadata.claim: POR executes when BOTH VDD and VDDIO are established. Default primary interface after reset/power-up is I2C; CSB held high retains I2C. A CSB RISING edge after power-up selects SPI after the stated200µs interval, until reset/next power-up. Manufacturer recommends an initial CHIP_ID SPI read with invalid returned value to generate this transition; NV_CONF.spi_en is a separately documented permanent-SPI alternative, not adopted here. Table1 tPO MAX2ms is supply-on to operational interface, distinct from the200µs selection interval and not full sensor/configuration readiness. Static CSB-to-GND alone is NOT the selection event. Each physical device needs its own valid interface state; applying this to all six is a project consequence, not a Bosch six-sensor startup implementation.

Supports mode00 (CPOL0/CPHA0) and11 (CPOL1/CPHA1), automatically distinguished using SCK after CSB falls. Default SPI configuration is4-wire; IF_CONF.spi3 enables3-wire. CSB active low starts communication; rising CSB ends it. SDO remains high-impedance throughout the4-wire WRITE cycle. Read description/Fig13 require a dummy byte before useful returned register data; do not mistake p124's generic16-bit sentence for the complete Fig13 read transaction. This is not a quantified bus-release-time or powered-off-output guarantee and does not certify six-device bus contention behavior.

Table19: fSPI MAX10MHz with maximum SDI or SDO load30pF and VDDIO≥1.62V; separate VDDIO<1.62V row MAX7MHz. SCK high/low MIN45ns at≥1.62V and MIN66ns at<1.62V. SDI setup/hold MIN20ns each; CSB setup/hold MIN40ns each. SDO delay MAX30ns at30pF/VDDIO≥1.62V. Idle after read any mode MIN2µs; after write normal/fast-startup MIN2µs; after write suspend/low-power MIN450µs. Table heading says timing valid at VDDIO≥1.62V although explicit lower-voltage clock/pulse rows are included; do not extrapolate unspecified lower-voltage output-delay guarantees. These are conditioned limits, not an unconditional10MHz six-device-bus qualification or a selected system clock/ODR.

Exact order codes ESP32-S3-WROOM-1-N8R2 and ESP32-S3-WROOM-1U-N8R2 each have8MB Quad-SPI flash and2MB Quad-SPI PSRAM; recommended module ambient range−40…85°C. WROOM-1 has a PCB antenna; WROOM-1U has an external antenna connector. Both use ESP32-S3 with512KB on-chip SRAM and native Wi-Fi/BLE. These are documented candidates, not adopted SKUs or proof of application memory/timing sufficiency.

WROOM-1/1U expose36 GPIO labels, GPIO0–21 and35–48, in41 module pins including EPAD/GND. USB_D−/D+ are GPIO19/20 at pads13/14; UART0 TX/RX GPIO43/44 at pads37/36; EN pad3 must not float. Boot-related GPIO0/3/45/46 require reset/eFuse-aware allocation. Table3-1 footnote b reserves GPIO35/36/37 for Octal-PSRAM variants, not the R2 Quad-PSRAM candidates; footnote c assigns GPIO47/48 to1.8V on ESP32-S3R16V-based variants. Pin defaults can depend on eFuse. A GPIO-label count is not proof of interchangeable direction/ADC/PWM/peripheral resources or a qualified full-board map; no silent suffix substitution.

GPIO19/20 carry USB D−/D+; U0TXD/U0RXD correspond to GPIO43/44. Octal-memory R8/R16V modules consume GPIO35/36/37; N8R2's Quad configuration must not be silently exchanged for R8. Straps GPIO0/3/45/46 default respectively weak pull-up/floating/weak pull-down/weak pull-down. SPI boot requires GPIO0 high; joint download requires GPIO0 low and GPIO46 low. Strap setup minimum0ms/hold minimum3ms about EN; eFuse-dependent VDD_SPI/JTAG/default-pad behavior remains conditional. eFuses are one-time programmable; no burn or complete pin-map approval follows. See existing DS-MCU-102 for module pad availability.

ESP32-S3 has TWO hardware I2C controllers. SDA/SCL are bidirectional open-drain lines requiring pullups; GPIO configuration is supported. Standard100kHz/Fast400kHz modes are documented, with master SCL not exceeding400kHz. Three physical pin pairs do not create a third hardware controller: software servicing or separately validated remapping remains Circuit/Firmware work.

Joint Download Boot supports UART0 downloading into flash or SRAM. Default ROM printing uses UART0 and USB Serial/JTAG; register/eFuse configuration can change or disable it. Silence is not proof of failed power/boot. Existing DS-MCU-102/120/121 retain pad/strap/reset facts. Capability is not a selected baud/protocol, implemented application logging, enabled recovery/security state or dedicated hardware debug connector.

original_evidence_metadata.section: Sections2.2/2.3/2.4; Table2-1 notes5/6, IO MUX continuation and Table2-10
original_evidence_metadata.claim: SoC pins49/U0TXD and50/U0RXD map GPIO43/44 and show WPU+IE both at and after reset: weak pull-up and input enabled, not an EN-low/unpowered leakage guarantee. GPIO19/20 are silicon pins25/26 on VDD3P3_RTC; GPIO20 has USB_PU in both reset columns, while GPIO19's cells are blank. Note6 distinguishes USB-controlled pulls/default USB function from weak GPIO pulls; disabling USB defaults weak GPIO pulls off. Module land numbers remain DS-MCU-102, not silicon pin numbers or a separately accessible PHY supply. CHIP_PU LOW disables the chip per Table2-10; this does not remove the external rail or define pad Ioff, Hi-Z, injection tolerance, actual runtime state or a safe power-up waveform.

original_evidence_metadata.section: Register33.3 USB_SERIAL_JTAG_CONF0_REG, reset row and field descriptions
original_evidence_metadata.claim: Documented reset fields: PHY_SEL=0,USB_PAD_ENABLE=1,DP_PULLUP=1,DM_PULLUP=0,PAD_PULL_OVERRIDE=0,EXCHG_PINS=0 and EXCHG_PINS_OVERRIDE=0. These are conditional hardware register defaults, not a measured pin waveform, actual configuration or VBUS-aware gate. VREFH control range1.76..2.00V/80mV steps and VREFL0.80..1.04V/80mV steps describe configurable single-ended threshold controls, not all-corner receiver limits or general GPIO VIH/VIL. Existing power-up fluctuation caveat DS-MCU-138 remains.

**SLVSCP6H conditional command/state semantics.** Powered DIR change stops electrical drive and restarts the motor-start sequencer; this is not instantaneous mechanical stopping. ISDen=1 measures BEMF in Hi-Z/coast: stationary judgment proceeds to BrkEn; forward rotation can resynchronize directly to ClosedLoop; reverse speed above RvsDrThr returns to ISD/coast; below threshold RvsDrEn=1 reverse-drives through zero then accelerates, whereas RvsDrEn=0 proceeds to BrkEn. ISDen=0 bypasses ISD to BrkEn, not a qualified high-speed workaround. Enabled Brake applies all three low-side FETs; after the configured interval, IPD or Align precedes acceleration. No dedicated BRAKE pin or generic runtime BRAKE trigger is defined in the complete pin/register tables. Configuring a duration is not documented as an immediate Brake-entry event; stop time, holding, repeatability and three-channel synchronization are not guaranteed. Source discrepancy retained: p22 calls RvsDrThr [2:0], but p24 and Table9 p45 define [1:0], address0x23 bits1:0; clarification remains pending rather than silently assuming three bits.
